name: s70-quality-gate-late-pass-keeps-newer-failure
setup_commands: export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR='{TMPROOT}'; H='{KIT_ROOT}/.claude/hooks/quality-gate.sh'; printf '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' '{TMPROOT}/src/a.py' | bash "$H" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 2; printf 'def y(:\n' > src/b.py; printf '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' '{TMPROOT}/src/b.py' | bash "$H" >/dev/null 2>&1; wait
notes: A slow scope-wide check starts on a.py while b.py is valid. b.py then breaks and its own run fails. When the slow run finishes it passed — on content it never saw. It used to overwrite the scope's result and re-hash b.py as verified, so stop was allowed. A run now records nothing once a later run of its scope has started, and re-covers only files unchanged since it started.
